text: In 1902, the French paid people in Hanoi to kill rats... so people started farming them.
Hanoi is the shiny new capital of French Indochina,
and the French just gave it a brand-new sewer system.
The rats love it.
It's a highway under every street, straight into the nicest houses.
And with plague spreading, a rat in your kitchen isn't just gross.
It's dangerous.
So the French send hunters down into the sewers.
Thousands of rats a day.
It's not enough.
So they make a new rule: anyone can hunt, and they'll pay one cent per rat.
But nobody at city hall wants a mountain of dead rats on their desk.
So: just bring the tail.
Tails pour in.
Tens of thousands.
The officials are thrilled.
Then someone notices something strange running down the street.
A rat.
With no tail.
Then another.
And another.
You see, a dead rat pays you once.
But a live rat without a tail keeps having babies, and every baby comes with a brand-new tail.
It's like getting paid for every egg... and then killing the chicken.
Nobody does that.
Soon, farms outside the city are breeding rats just for the reward.
The French finally cancel the reward.
And the man who built those sewers, Paul Doumer, goes home... and later becomes President of France.
The rats?
They stayed.
